findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine fail to reach the minimum required temperature for sanitizing (160F) during today’s inspection. The dish machine appears to complete the wash step and fail to complete the rinse step, which is the high-temperature step of the process. The PIC was made aware of the issue and has requested service on the machine. In the meantime, staff are placing dishes from the dish machine into a triple sink basin of quaternary ammonia sanitizer. A follow-up will be conducted on September 14, 2026 to ensure the dish machine has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant to the left of the dish machine to be damaged and soiled. Ensure this sealant is repaired or replaced to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Light was observed passing through the gap beneath the exit door in the dinning area.The inspector advised the person-in-charge (PIC) to use a weather stripping to seal the gap so as to prevent entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Dust accumulation was observed on the fan covers in both walk-in coolers.
2. Soil accumulation (icy shade) was observed beneath the fan casing in the walk-in coolers by the dish self.

The inspector instructed the PIC to have the fan covers and fan casing cleaned to sight and touch so as to prevent contamination of foods stored in the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two separate storage order violations in the walk-in cooler. Raw pork was stored in a bin with deli meat, and cooked chicken was stored in a bin with raw chicken. The PIC was informed and the contaminated items were discarded. Inspector conducted education while onsite regarding storage order. The cooler does have a storage order flyer posted. Ensure staff are supervising volunteers during food storage to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed cutlery and dining trays to be stored with their food-contact surfaces face-up with no adequate coverings. PIC was informed that the food-contact surfaces of items need to be covered or inverted to protect from cross-contamination. All items were inverted during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mops to be stored with their mop heads on the floor. The PIC was informed that mops need to be stored such that they can safely drip dry to prevent bacterial accumulation and cross-contamination. All mops were properly inverted during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: Inspector observed four pans of eggs cooling in the walk in covered with pan lids. The lids were turned so that the heat can escape. The pan lids were twisted and pans separated. Ensure to develop a good habit and use proper cooling techniques. 

(A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: Inspector observes doors from the outside into the facility have gaps and cracks. The pest control company has had this on their list of client responsibilities. The PCO is doing service every two weeks. Follow all directions from the pest control company to completely eliminate pests. 

(A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13:  Inspector showed manager several areas where the base cove has holes, gaps and or broken or missing tile. Repiar these areas and ensure that they are maintained sealed. This will help in the control of pests. 

(A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Sliced deli meats are observed in the walk in #2. Deli meats are not date marked. Ensure that all foods taken in are properly date marked. The items were received yesterday. The packages were properly date marked today. The violation is considered corrected on site. 


3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Inspector observed a large fan blocking the approach to the hand sink. The fan was pushed back. Do not allow anything to block the approach to the hand sink. The violation is considered corrected at the time of service.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Inspector observed a partial two liter of Fanta to be sitting on the prep table. The soda was removed to the garbage. Store personal drinks and personal food items on table where other employee drinks are located. The violation is considered corrected at time of inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed sani bucket in the kitchen to have 0 ppm. Bleach had lost concentration. Bleach bucket was remade - 200 ppm. Discussed frequent changes of sani bucket to ensure concentration stays 50-200 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed both walk-in cooler fans to have dust and debris. Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces. Ensure area is cleaned before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed large metal shelving unit used to hold dried cooking utensils (in front of men’s employee bathroom) to have large accumulation of chipped paint and rust. Replace this shelving unit before next routine inspection and/or reseal with paint.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces in need of cleaning due to dust and debris:
1. Walk-in cooler fans have accumulation of dust.
2. Spray nozzle of 3 dish machine has accumulation of grime and food debris on top of handle area.
3. Shelving unit of clean dish ware near the walk-in coolers is dusty.

Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces before next routine inspection. These items were noted in the general comments of the last routine inspection on 2/4/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repair due to no longer being smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulking at dish machine in front of spray nozzle - in need of caulking.
2. Mop utility sink in need of caulking around top where sink and wall meet.
3. Duct tape attached to handle of walk-in cooler #2 (where milk and cooled items were being held). Cease practice. Repair so smooth and easily cleanable.

Ensure all repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. Reference 4-302.14.

Observed facility to lack a method to test heat dish machine. Discussed purchasing heat test strips and/or a maximum registering thermometer. Inspector will follow-up on 2/14/20.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed eating in the food preparation area. Open drinks observed on prep surfaces. All drinks were discarded. Provide and use designated area outside for eating. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) cole slaw is 55°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was served or discarded before the 4 hour. Also observed dressing on the salad bar or open on the sid table not under refrigeration. Dressings were also discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) Salad is 50°F. When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19. All items on the salad bar are discarded at the end of the serving period. Salad bar is set up between 12 and 12:30pm and is discarded by 3:55pm.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Observed wet wiping cloths to be stored in sanitizer soultion that is less than 200ppm of quat. The sanitizer buckets were remade with the sanitizer dispenser at the 3 part sink. Discussed the use of cotton cloths with the sanitabs and soaking the cloths in sanitizer before putting them into the sanitizer buckets. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution between uses. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:

750-160bGloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations.

findings.comment:

750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed cheese sauce with a date of 7/21/2018. This is beyond the seven days. Any potentially hazardous foods must be used or discarded within seven days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.comment:
Observed two containers of soup in the walk in cooler without a proper label.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
Label with the time & date, all potentially hazardous food that you prepare that requires refrigeration.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed two large covered containers of soup at 117F in the walk in cooler.  Per Ms. Barger, the soup was made at the facility and placed in the cooler about an hour ago.
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.
Properly cool food by limiting depth to no greater than 4", using an ice bath, paddles, etc.  Corrected:  The soup was transferred to large shallow pans and an ice bath placed in the center of the pans.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Repeat: Observed cracked caulk at the hand sink in the women restroom.  
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable.
Recaulk the sink to the wall.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Did not observe any concentration of chlorine in the sanitizer container.
750-800c Where equipment and utensils are used for the preparation of  potentially hazardous foods on a continuous or production-line basis, utensils and the food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized at intervals throughout the day on a schedule subject to the approval of the regulatory authority.  This schedule shall be based on food temperature, type of food, and amount of food particle accumulation.
Provide a solution of 100 - 200ppm for choline for surface sanitizing.  Corrected:  The solution was remixed to 100ppm chlorine.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following to be soiled:
1.Fan guards in the reach in cooler,  2.Back side of the ovens, 3.walk in cooler shelves.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean the shelves and maintain clean.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Did not observe an air gap for the ice maker.  
750-290 Ice storage bins shall be drained through an air gap. Provide an air gap.
Provide an air gap to prevent backflow.  Corrected:  A plastic tub was used to elevate the drain line, temporarily.  Provide a permanent solution.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed several dented cans on the can racks.  Set aside for return or discard severely dented cans.  Corrected:  The cans were discarded.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed cooked and cooled turkeys in the walk in cooler without a proper label.  Label with the TIME and DATE, all potentially hazardous food that requires refrigeration.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed cracked caulk at the hand sink in the women's restroom.  Recaulk the sink to the wall.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed food splatter on the inside top and sides of the microwave.  Clean and sanitize the inside of the microwave.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the ice maker draining to the floor.  Direct the ice melt to a drain.
750-1100(b) Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Did not observe a lid for the waste can in the men's restroom.  Provide a trash can with a lid.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor soiled in the following locations: 1.under the 3-compartment sink, 2.under the auto dish machine, 3.behind the soup kettle, 4.under the coffee area.  Clean the floor and maintain clean.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Did not observe an air gap for the ice maker.  Provide an air gap for the ice bin.  Corrected: drain was repositioned.
750-290 Ice storage bins shall be drained through an air gap. Provide an air gap.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Observed ice in the hand sink.  Use the hand sink only for hand washing.  Corrected:  Discussed with the manager.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed unwashed apples above ready to eat food.  Store unwashed produce below ready to eat food.  Apples were removed from the cooler and washed.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed duct tape on storage shelves and at the coffee maker.  Remove the tape.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed a build-up of soil around the can opener.  Clean this area.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
In the walkin freezer,frozen raw hamburger stored over the top of fully cooked meats. (corrected)
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.
